mainTopic: נותן טעם לפגם: when a forbidden food gives flavor that makes the mixture worse
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוחנן's rule about mixtures. If you can taste the forbidden food but its substance is gone, the mixture is forbidden, but there are no מלקות. If the forbidden food made the flavor worse, the mixture is permitted. The גמרא explains that his word ריבה ('increased') teaches something extra: the mixture is permitted even if other things also helped spoil the taste. The גמרא then rules like the second version of ריש לקיש. רב כהנא says all the אמוראים agree that נותן טעם לפגם is מותר, but אביי objects that ריש לקיש may only have been quoting others. The גמרא asks whether anyone forbids a spoiling taste, and a ברייתא answers yes: רבי מאיר forbids it, while רבי שמעון permits it. רבי מאיר learns from גיעולי גוים, and the two תנאים argue over whether a קדירה בת יומא already spoils the taste a little. The amud ends as the גמרא begins רבי שמעון's own source, a ברייתא on the פסוק about נבלה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: flavor without substance, and flavor that spoils
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יוחנן's rule. Flavor without substance is forbidden but has no מלקות. If the forbidden food made the flavor worse, the mixture is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only its flavor is there but not its actual substance, it is forbidden, but there are no lashes for it. And if it added flavor that spoils the food, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement of רבי יוחנן that started just before this section. It describes two more levels of a mixture that contains forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן ruled that when both the flavor and the substance are present, the food is forbidden and one gets מלקות. Here the substance is gone and only the flavor remains, so it is still אסור but there are no מלקות. If the forbidden food actually made the taste worse (טעם לפגם), the mixture becomes מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Flavor that spoils or worsens the food

phrases.english: Its flavor but not its substance: forbidden,
but one is not given lashes for it,
and if it increased the flavor to its detriment: permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flavor without substance is אסור but has no מלקות. Flavor that worsens the mixture makes it מותר.

steps.title: Why say 'increased' instead of 'gave flavor'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's wording. Why didn't he just say 'if it gave flavor that spoils, it is permitted'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say: if it gave flavor to its detriment, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording רבי יוחנן used. It suggests a simpler way he could have said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual phrase is נותן טעם לפגם, 'gives flavor that spoils.' רבי יוחנן said ריבה, 'increased,' instead. The גמרא assumes every word is there for a reason, so it asks what this word is adding.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא: אִם נָתַן טַעַם לִפְגָם — מוּתָּר!
phrases.english: But let him say: if it gave flavor to its detriment, it is permitted!

steps.kashyaTarget: The word ריבה in רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain phrase 'נתן טעם' would have been enough, so the extra word seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Other things that also spoiled the taste
steps.stepSummary: The word 'increased' teaches a new point. The mixture is permitted even if other things also helped spoil the taste along with the forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: even though there are other things that spoiled it together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the wording. 'Increased' means the forbidden food added to spoiling that other things were also causing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the היתר only applies when the forbidden food alone ruined the taste. The word ריבה teaches that even when other ingredients also worsened the flavor, the forbidden food's part in the spoiling still makes the mixture מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא מִילֵּי אַחְרָנְיָיתָא
phrases.english: that even though there are other things
that spoiled it along with it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word teaches a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mixture is permitted only if the forbidden food by itself spoiled the taste.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is permitted even when other ingredients also helped spoil the taste.

steps.title: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש's second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows the second version of ריש לקיש's statement from earlier in the sugya.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows the last version of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling. Of the two versions of ריש לקיש's statement quoted earlier, we follow the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא recorded two versions (לישני) of what ריש לקיש said about נותן טעם לפגם. This line settles which version is the practical הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the second version of ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows the last version of Reish Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ruling that refers back to ריש לקיש's statement from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We rule like ריש לקיש's second version.

steps.title: רב כהנא: everyone agrees spoiling flavor is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that all the אמוראים quoted agree that נותן טעם לפגם is מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: From the words of all of them we learn that flavor that spoils is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא sums up the sugya. Every opinion quoted shows that flavor which spoils the food is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא looks across all the statements (שמואל, רבי יוחנן, ריש לקיש). He sees that each one assumes נותן טעם לפגם מותר, so he treats it as a rule everyone holds.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of all of them

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
From the words of all of them we learn
that flavor given to its detriment is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִדִּבְרֵי כּוּלָּם נִלְמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that gathers all the earlier opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the quoted אמוראים agree that נותן טעם לפגם is מותר.

steps.title: אביי: ריש לקיש may only have been quoting
steps.stepSummary: אביי agrees about the other אמוראים but not about ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש only said 'they said,' so he may not hold this himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Granted, from all the others this works well. But ריש לקיש says 'they said,' and he himself does not hold it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on part of רב כהנא's claim. He argues that ריש לקיש cannot be counted as agreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש opened with 'they did not say נותן טעם לפגם is permitted except...'. That wording shows he was reporting what others ruled, not giving his own view. So רב כהנא cannot say everyone agrees.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Granted, from all of them it is fine,
but as for Reish Lakish:
he says 'they said,'
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש opened with 'they did not say...', which sounds like he was quoting other people's ruling.

phrases.english: and he himself does not hold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא מִכּוּלְּהוּ לְחַיֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects part of the proof in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inclusion of ריש לקיש; the other אמוראים still count as agreeing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'אמרו' means ריש לקיש was quoting others, so his own view is unknown.

steps.title: Does anyone forbid spoiling flavor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב כהנא had to prove this from everyone, does that mean some opinion forbids נותן טעם לפגם?
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, is there someone who says that flavor which spoils is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next discussion. It asks whether רב כהנא's statement implies that someone actually holds נותן טעם לפגם is אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stressing that 'everyone' permits it suggests that someone might disagree. The גמרא now asks who that could be. The next step answers this with a ברייתא.

phrases.english: By implication, is there someone who says:
flavor given to its detriment is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from רב כהנא's statement in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who, if anyone, holds that נותן טעם לפגם is אסור.

steps.title: Yes, a ברייתא shows a תנא who forbids a spoiling taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא: רבי מאיר forbids both a spoiling taste and an improving taste, while רבי שמעון forbids only an improving taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and a ברייתא teaches: Whether the forbidden food makes the taste worse or makes it better, the mixture is forbidden. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says: If it makes the taste better, it is forbidden. If it makes the taste worse, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step: yes, there is an opinion that forbids נותן טעם לפגם. It is רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב כהנא worked hard to show that all the אמוראים permit נותן טעם לפגם. That suggested someone disagrees. The ברייתא names him: רבי מאיר forbids it, and רבי שמעון permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden food that gives a bad, spoiling taste to the mixture
Forbidden food that gives a good, improving taste to the mixture

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole מחלוקת. The rest of this section explains the reasoning of רבי מאיר and of רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Yes, and indeed it is taught in a ברייתא:
Both where it gives a taste that spoils
and where it gives a taste that improves —
it is forbidden; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי שמעון says:
If it improves, it is forbidden; if it spoils, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7 by naming a תנא who forbids נותן טעם לפגם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there an opinion that forbids נותן טעם לפגם?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי מאיר forbids it, and רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns from the pots of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's reason. He learns from גיעולי גוים: their taste is already spoiled, yet the תורה still forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason? He learns it from the pots of non-Jews that need purging. Don't the pots of non-Jews give a spoiling taste? And yet the Merciful One forbade them. So too here, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר forbids a spoiling taste, and answers that he learns it from the pots of non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew's pot that was used in the past gives off an old, stale taste, which is a spoiling taste. Even so, the תורה requires the pot to be purged before use. רבי מאיר concludes that a spoiling taste still forbids food.

keyTerms.meaning: Pots of non-Jews that must be purged before a Jew may use them
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
He learns it from the pots of non-Jews that need purging.

phrases.aramaic: גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם לָאו נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם הוּא?
phrases.english: Don't the pots of non-Jews give a spoiling taste?
And yet the Merciful One forbade them.
So too here, there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for רבי מאיר's opinion from Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source for רבי מאיר's ruling that a spoiling taste is forbidden?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גיעולי גוים: their taste is spoiled, yet the תורה forbids them.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the תורה only forbade a pot used that same day
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rejects the proof. Following רב הונא בריה דרב חייא, the תורה only forbade a קדירה בת יומא, and its taste is not spoiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי שמעון)? He holds like רב הונא son of רב חייא, who said: The תורה only forbade a pot used that same day, whose taste is not spoiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי שמעון answers רבי מאיר's proof from the pots of non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר assumed the forbidden pots give a spoiling taste. רבי שמעון says the תורה only forbade a pot used within the last day, whose taste is still good. So the pots are no proof that a spoiling taste is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning how does the other opinion answer this?
A pot used for cooking within the last day

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי שמעון: how does he deal with רבי מאיר's proof?

phrases.english: He holds like רב הונא son of רב חייא,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: as רב הונא son of רב חייא said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קְדֵירָה בַּת יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: The תורה only forbade a pot used that same day,
whose taste is not spoiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? כִּדְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's proof from Step 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pots the תורה forbade are only those used within the last day, which do not give a spoiling taste.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: even a same-day pot spoils the taste a little
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר defends his proof. Even a קדירה בת יומא always spoils the taste a little, so the תורה did forbid a somewhat spoiling taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי מאיר)? Even a pot used that same day cannot help spoiling the taste a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי מאיר answers back and keeps his proof alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר can accept that the תורה only forbade a same-day pot. But he says even that pot spoils the taste slightly. Since the תורה still forbade it, a spoiling taste is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון both agree the תורה forbade a same-day pot. They disagree about whether that pot already spoils the taste a little.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now it means רבי מאיר: how does he answer רבי שמעון?

phrases.english: Even a pot used that same day
cannot help spoiling the taste a little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי מאיר's proof against רבי שמעון's rejection in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A same-day pot gives a fully good taste, so it proves nothing about a spoiling taste.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a same-day pot spoils the taste slightly, so the proof still stands.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's own source: the פסוק about נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to give רבי שמעון's source. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that only what is fit for a גר is called נבלה. The explanation continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי שמעון's reason? As a ברייתא teaches: "Do not eat any נבלה; give it to the גר who is in your gates." Whatever is fit for a גר is called נבלה,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for רבי שמעון's own source and begins to answer with a ברייתא about נבלה. This sets up an argument that finishes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the ban on נבלה to the fact that a גר could eat it. The ברייתא learns that only meat fit for a גר to eat counts as forbidden נבלה. The next lines will show that spoiled meat is not forbidden, which supports permitting a spoiling taste.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Here, a non-Jew living among Jews (גר תושב)

steps.confusionAlert: Here גר does not mean a convert. It means a non-Jew who lives among the Jews, to whom one may give נבלה.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון, what is his reason?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Do not eat any animal that died without שחיטה;
to the non-Jew who is in your gates" (you may give it).
whatever is fit for a non-Jew is called נבלה,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the debate over רבי מאיר's source, the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's own positive source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי שמעון's source for permitting a spoiling taste?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא on דברים 14:21: only what is fit for a גר is called נבלה. The argument is completed in the next lines.
